candidates.title: Prepare a delayed-shipment alert

demandEvidence.chore: Notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: A simple flow can notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable alert draft identifying a potentially delayed shipment and the supplied reason.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a new status record or starts a test run with a synthetic shipment record.
steps: Accept a synthetic shipment record and its timestamp.
Compare the supplied status and time with the operator-defined delay rule.
Mark the record as possibly delayed when the rule matches.
Prepare an alert draft containing only the supplied identifier and status.
Have an operator verify the result and decide whether to send it.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a small labeled set of synthetic status records, verify that records meeting the written delay rule produce an alert draft and other records do not.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator must supply and validate status data and the delay rule, review every alert, and authorize any external notification; no live carrier or logistics connection is evidenced.
unverified: No supplied reference documents event ingestion or notification delivery for this task.
The discussion does not specify status fields, delay rules, volume, recurrence, or access to shipment systems.
No Make or n8n execution, external endpoint, or deployment is established.

ease.reason: A synthetic rule-and-alert mock is approachable, but no attached source documents an implementation path for the task.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: ecommerce operations teams may value delay alerts; this discussion establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic alert draft is bounded; carrier data access and live delivery are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A supplied status can be checked repeatedly in a proposal, but no event connector is documented and a person must verify and send alerts.

evidence.reason: The retained task span names a delayed-shipment dispatcher alert; it gives no fields, recurrence, buyer evidence, or implementation support.

candidates.reason: The retained task span supports a narrow synthetic alert-drafting experiment. Mean 5.0 is below the threshold; no supplied implementation reference supports event intake or delivery.

candidates.title: Draft booking status notifications

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare booking confirmations and service-provider assignment notifications.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: automate booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications

experimentPlan.output: A human-reviewable booking confirmation draft from a supplied fictional booking and provider assignment.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a fictional booking and assignment record for a test run.
steps: Check that required test fields are present.
Match the booking to the supplied provider assignment.
Fill an approved template with the supplied booking details.
Flag missing or conflicting fields instead of guessing.
Ask an operator to verify and authorize the draft.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use labeled fictional records, including missing and conflicting assignments, and verify that complete records produce accurate drafts while ambiguous records are flagged for review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person must supply and confirm booking data, verify assignments, approve every message, and handle any payment or customer record; the source does not establish access to a live application.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference documents booking-event intake or message delivery.
The discussion does not provide a schema, booking system, authentication details, or operating volume.
Payment status correctness, duplicate suppression, retries, and external API execution are unverified.

ease.reason: A template-filling mock can use fictional records, but the attached discussion alone does not document its implementation mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: on-demand service operators may value fewer manual booking messages; this question establishes no payment evidence.

feasibility.reason: A four-week fictional confirmation draft is narrow; live booking access, payment status, and reliable delivery remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: Template preparation can repeat on supplied records, while a person must validate assignments and authorize messages; no connector is documented.

evidence.reason: The retained post span explicitly asks about booking confirmations and provider assignment notices, but provides no schema or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: The full retained span supports a bounded fictional confirmation-drafting experiment. Mean 4.8 is below threshold; live booking, payment, retry, and notification mechanics are not evidenced.

candidates.title: Organize scattered trip details

demandEvidence.chore: Gather trip details that are scattered across a spreadsheet, airline apps, inboxes, and a photo library.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: My trips were scattered across a spreadsheet, airline apps, old inboxes and a photo library

experimentPlan.output: A single reviewable trip summary assembled from operator-supplied fictional travel snippets.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator manually submits a small set of fictional trip snippets for organization.
steps: Accept only supplied synthetic text snippets.
Extract proposed date, place, and reservation label fields.
Group fields under the operator-supplied trip name.
Mark missing or conflicting details without filling them in.
Have an operator compare the summary with the original snippets.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Compare each proposed field with labeled synthetic source snippets and confirm that missing or conflicting details are flagged rather than inferred.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person must supply and verify all details; this experiment does not connect to inboxes, airline apps, spreadsheets, or photo libraries and must not ingest real traveler records.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference documents extraction or integrations for this task.
The post describes the author's scattered information but gives no recurring frequency, other buyer evidence, or exact fields.
Accuracy across real booking formats and any external account access remain untested.

ease.reason: A manual synthetic-input summary can be outlined, but no attached source documents extraction or integration capability.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: frequent travelers might value trip organization, but this maker statement does not establish a paying customer or demand from service firms.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic text organizer is possible as a proposal; real inbox, airline, spreadsheet, and photo integrations are outside the evidence.

autonomy.reason: The proposed version depends on manual input and verification, and no automated source collection is documented.

evidence.reason: The public post explicitly describes trip details scattered across four sources, but is one maker's statement with no frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: A narrow synthetic trip-summary experiment follows the stated organization problem. Mean 4.0 is below threshold; the post provides no evidence of a professional-services buyer or integrations.
